FIX BUG #368: Without --repo, the ship drift, dirty-tree and gate-head guards can never fire

You are fixing exactly one bug from the code-health epic (#330) on branch fix-368-repo-guards, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text is below and is the whole framing: its "Fix" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Where the issue says the operator rules between options, implement the option the issue recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say in your result notes which option you took so the pull request can ask for the ruling.

RULES
- Scope: fix this bug and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites.
- Tests: add or extend the suite that proves the fix. Assert exact values and exact error variants or text, never is_err() alone. Show every new test binds: make a compiling mutation that removes the fix, run the test and see it fail, restore the fix, and record the failing test name in your notes.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new line and branch reachable by a test. If a branch cannot be reached deterministically, restructure rather than leave it uncovered.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Gates before you report complete, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test for every crate you touched (crate-scoped: cargo test -p <crate>); git diff --check.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#368)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

THE ISSUE (#368), verbatim:

Found by the code-health sweep (epic #330). Verified on `main` at `ba52724e` (2026-09-25).

## What happens

`Engine.repo` is `Option<PathBuf>` (`crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs:176`). When `--repo` is omitted:

- Seats run and commit in `workdir()`, which falls back to the current directory (`engine.rs:982-988`: `self.repo.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| std::env::current_dir()…)`).
- **Every git fact the engine owns is gated on `self.repo` being `Some`** (`engine.rs:489`, `:699`, `:959`, `:1158`, `:2213`, `:2693`, `:4726`). With `None` the engine skips all of them:
  - gate-head arming: start and end both read `None`, so **GATE-MOVED-HEAD cannot fire**
  - `reviewed_heads`
  - `fixes_docs_only`
  - ship's `dirty_worktrees` and `drift_detected`
  - anchor and keep-refs

In `recipes/fast/policy.json`, `SHIP-DRIFT {drift_detected: true}` and `SHIP-DIRTY {dirty_worktrees: true}` then **can never match**, so a run reaches `SHIP-READY` or `SHIP-COMPLETE` without those checks. The engine computes an `operated` repository for the boundary fence at start (`:328-336`) and then discards it.

`docs/guides/quickstart.md:270` says `--repo` defaults to the current directory, and that is true for where seats work. It is not true for the guards.

## Why it matters

The drift, dirty-tree and moved-head protections switch off silently depending on a CLI flag. That is fail-open on the ship path. No test pins this as intended; the only statement of it is a comment ("no repository, no head").

## Fix

- Introduce a value object: resolve `OperatedRepo(PathBuf)` once at construction (the `operated` path already computed) and use it for both `workdir()` and every git fact.
- Or make `--repo` required.
- If the `None` path is deliberate, the operator rules it and the engine then **refuses** to ship without a repository instead of skipping the guards.

## Acceptance

- A run started without `--repo` in a dirty worktree parks on SHIP-DIRTY exactly as a run with `--repo .` does. A test proves it.
- A gate seat that moves HEAD parks with GATE-MOVED-HEAD in both modes.

created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes:
Fixed #368 using the issue's first option (resolve the operated repository once), not the 'make --repo required' option and not 'refuse to ship without a repository'. The PR should ask the operator to confirm that ruling. The value object is the field type itself: Engine.repo went from Option<PathBuf> to PathBuf, set by a new operated_repo(Option<PathBuf>) helper (the --repo named, else current_dir) in start_in_world, start_with_dispatch and resume. workdir(), gate-head arming at both sites and its end check, phase/entered head, reviewed_heads, fixes_docs_only, ship dirty_worktrees/drift_detected, house_rules, the anchor and keep-refs all read that one path. I added no newtype. Committed 6da953ed, signed (%G? = G, steward key) with Signed-off-by and the Co-Authored-By trailer last. Not pushed.

TEST: crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/operated_repo.rs, one test in its own binary because it calls set_current_dir: without_repo_the_guards_read_the_directory_the_run_stands_in. In each mode (Some(".") = --repo ., and None) it asserts that a dirty worktree ends (Stopped, SHIP-DIRTY) and that a gate driver which commits ends (AwaitingOperator, GATE-MOVED-HEAD). It passes on the fix.

BINDING: I restored the original engine.rs from HEAD with the new test kept. The test failed in 'none' mode with left (Completed, Some("SHIP-READY")) and right (Stopped, Some("SHIP-DIRTY")), which is the bug exactly. I then skipped the dirty assertion temporarily, and the gate half failed on its own in 'none' mode with left (Completed, SHIP-READY) and right (AwaitingOperator, GATE-MOVED-HEAD). The fix and the test were then restored.

SIDE EFFECT FOUND AND HANDLED: with the fix, tests that started or resumed with repo None and drove to a conclusion began anchoring into this checkout, because cargo's cwd is inside the worktree. My first runs planted 12 refs in the shared repo: refs/forge/{feature-fresh-start-bbcd344e, feature-mid-phase-1bf5f84e, crash-test-ae571048, crash-test-fe8892a8, between, boundary, mid, bound-run, bound-run-2, stopped-mid-flight} plus two refs/forge/keep/feature-*/ba52724e... keep-refs. I deleted exactly those with git update-ref -d. A diff of the full refs/forge list against the pre-run snapshot is now empty. Those tests now name their tempdir: recovery.rs (both tests), two_engines_one_journal.rs (the child is spawned with current_dir(tempdir) so it keeps the no-repo path), engine/tests.rs an_accepted_operator_stop (resume), contention_tests (start), and brokkr-cli src/tests.rs (the dispatch run test and resume_concludes_an_accepted_but_unconcluded_operator_stop). Five engine unit tests that assigned engine.repo = Some(..) now assign the PathBuf directly.

GATES (run this session): cargo fmt --all -- --check clean. git diff --check clean. cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings finished with no warnings. cargo test -p brokkr-runtime: every suite ok (lib 488 passed, operated_repo 1 passed), and no new refs afterwards. cargo test -p brokkr-cli: all suites ok with the engine change (lib 468, driver_conformance 24, machine_proof 61, ...). After the CLI tests.rs edit I re-ran only --lib (468 passed, no new refs). cargo run -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self succeeded. No witness digest moved (witness_digests 4 passed, no re-pin). No frozen surface touched.

PENDING: scripts/coverage-exact.sh was not run, per the rules; the controller runs it. The new closure in workdir() (unwrap_or_else(|_| self.repo.clone())) is reached by the existing PathBuf::new() case in engine/tests.rs, and the operated_repo None branch is reached by operated_repo.rs and two_engines_one_journal. I did not measure this. Remote CI is also pending.

FOLLOW-UPS, not fixed: (1) The CLI still hands the engine repo: Option while it compiles against repo.unwrap_or(workspace). In production workspace is ".", so both resolve to cwd, but a caller that injects a workspace (the tests) gets a different tree. Passing Some(operated_repo) from the CLI would close that. (2) The gate tests in engine/tests.rs around line 914 wrap the capabilities message in a "body" object. The protocol Message is flattened: my own driver with that shape failed with 'missing field `driver`'. My unconfirmed guess is that a_gate_driver_that_commits_parks_with_raw_head_evidence passes only because its script commits after stdin closes. (3) docs/guides/quickstart.md:270 ('--repo defaults to the current directory') is now true for the guards as well, so I made no docs change.
